title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of a manuscript titled 'Connexions projectives canoniques et uniformisation des courbes algébriques'. Section 1 begins setting up projective connections functorially over an arbitrary base scheme S.

(1) A Brauer–Severi scheme P/S of constant relative dimension r is a proper smooth S-scheme whose geometric fibres are projective spaces. Giving one is the same as giving a torsor T under PGL(r+1)_S, which Grothendieck writes GP(r)_S. Here 'torsor' is meant in the étale or fppf topology.

(2) Giving a pair (P, σ) with σ a section amounts to reducing the structure group to the stabilizer of a fixed section of the model P^r_0 = P(O_S^{r+1}). The chosen section corresponds to the rank-one quotient O_S^{r+1} → O_S given by the last coordinate, using the EGA convention that P(E) parametrizes rank-one quotients. This stabilizer is the affine group Aff(r)_S = GL(r) ⋉ E^r, where E^r is the vector group G_a^r.

(3) Bracketed verification. Write O_S^{r+1} = E_0 × L_0 with E_0 = O^r as subobject and L_0 = O as quotient. The automorphisms of this module that respect the extension structure, taken modulo scalars, are the block matrices (A C; 0 1) with A in GL(r) and C in E^r. The page's brace labels give the matrix size r+1 and the block A size r.

(4) Consequently (P, σ) is equivalent to an extension 0 → Ω → E → O_S → 0 with Ω locally free of rank r. The functor is E ↦ (P(E), σ), where σ is the section defined by the quotient E → O_S. The next page asserts this functor is an equivalence of categories.

(5) Remarks on the notation Ω.
- σ*Ω^1_{P/S} ≅ ker(E → O_S) ⊗ σ*O(1)^{-1} = Ω, so Ω is the conormal sheaf J/J^2 of σ(S).
- The next page goes on to describe the infinitesimal neighbourhoods O_P/J^{n+1} as augmented O_S-algebras via Sym^n.

Purpose: this is the standard preliminary for defining a projective connection on a curve (or relative curve) X/S. Such a connection is a P^1-bundle with section, osculating X to infinite order along the diagonal, the rank-2 extension being of jet-bundle type. The aim is to discuss canonical projective connections coming from uniformization (Fuchsian or Schwarzian structures).
errors: No mathematical errors on the page itself.

The equivalence (P,σ) ↔ extensions holds only if morphisms of extensions are required to induce the identity on the quotient O_S. That normalization is exactly what the 'modulo scalars, last entry 1' condition encodes. It is implicit, not stated.
Notation: 'GP(r)' denotes PGL(r+1), indexed by relative dimension, not PGL(r).

Implicit point: a pointed Brauer–Severi scheme is Zariski-locally trivial and of the form P(E). This holds because Aff(r)-torsors are Zariski-locally trivial (Hilbert 90 for GL_r and for vector groups). It is consistent with the page but not said.

ideas.what: Brauer–Severi schemes of relative dimension r correspond to PGL(r+1)-torsors
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I (Dix exposés), SGA 3

ideas.what: A section of P reduces the structure group to the point stabilizer Aff(r) = GL(r) ⋉ G_a^r, the block matrices (A C; 0 1)
ideas.modern_name: Parabolic reduction / stabilizer of a point in PGL

ideas.what: Pointed Brauer–Severi schemes are equivalent to extensions 0→Ω→E→O_S→0, via P(E) with the section given by the quotient O_S; Ω is the conormal sheaf of the section
ideas.modern_name: Projective bundle with section / affine bundle as extension class

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only routine torsor and structure-group bookkeeping that sets up projective connections. Any interest lies in the later pages and in the title's programme: canonical projective connections and uniformization of algebraic curves done scheme-theoretically over a general base. That programme anticipates jet-bundle and oper-style formulations, but nothing on this page is new.
transcription_corrections: 'La donnée d'un P avec section σ [?] équivaut à se donner' — the image reads roughly 'avec section quelconque revient à se donner'; there is no σ symbol at that spot.
In the bracket: 'Le Groupe des automorphismes du Module O_S^{r+1} = O_S^r × O_S = E_0 × L_0 qui respectent la structure d'extension, modulo les matrices scalaires, est en effet celui des matrices'.
Matrix labels: left brace 'r+1' gives the full matrix size, right brace 'r' gives the size of block A.
